# SiteFile AI — Business Plan for Approval

**Prepared:** 8 October 2026
**Target:** R50,000 MRR from an AI-native, web-based subscription business
**Status:** Awaiting Michael's approval. Nothing has been bought, deployed or sent.

---

## 1. The call

**Build SiteFile AI: specification-matched health and safety files for South African subcontractors, generated by an agent, human-checked for the first 20, and billed per active site per month.**

The contractor uploads the principal contractor's own H&S specification, picks the site scope and high-risk tasks, and the agent produces the full Construction Regulations 2014 file: H&S plan, risk assessments, method statements, fall protection plan, emergency plan, appointment letters, registers, plus a clause-by-clause responsibility schedule and gap register that maps every clause of the specification to a response. Company documents (CIPC, COID letter of good standing, insurances, appointments, people, competencies, equipment) live in a vault and flow into every new file, so the second site takes ten minutes. Each live site gets a shareable, read-only file link with an audit log that the principal contractor can open at any time. That link is what keeps the subscription alive: the file stays live while the site is live.

This is the product we built by hand for Transnet in August (32-section file, 531-line audit responsibility schedule, submitted via Bayside Engineering). We know the buyer, the rejection reasons and the output standard. The durable moat is not the schedule, which any competitor can copy in weeks. It is the library of real principal contractor specifications (Transnet TPT, Toyota, Tiger Brands, Unilever, the retail rollout PCs) encoded as requirement registers, plus principal contractors adopting the share link as the way they receive files.

**Sequencing matters more than features.** We launch as an AI-powered, human-checked file service with 24-hour turnaround and the platform as our back office. The first five files go onto our own BCS sites, where we control the outcome. Self-serve download opens only after three principal contractors have accepted SiteFile output. This protects BCS's name on Durban sites and gives us cash and the spec library from week one.

## 2. Why this and not something else

| Candidate | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **Spec-matched safety file subscription (chosen)** | Real recurring pain, we hold the domain knowledge, our existing network is the first 20 customers, MVP is buildable in 2 days on Vercel + Supabase + Claude. |
| Bird/pest compliance monitoring SaaS for FMCG sites (Tiger Brands, Pepsico, Unilever) | Higher contract value but 3 to 6 month enterprise sales cycles. Becomes a module inside SiteFile later (same vault, same document engine). |
| Generic per-file safety file generator | Already crowded at R400 to R2,000 per file (MySafetyFile, Rapid Safety Files, SHe Files). Price-compressed, SEO-owned by incumbents. We do not compete there. |
| Generic AI agency, content, or consumer app (Snapboks) | No distribution, no moat, no MRR logic. |

## 3. Market evidence (from today's research)

- Every principal contractor must open and keep a site H&S file under Construction Regulation 7(1)(b), and every contractor must do the same for its own work under CR 7(2). Principal contractors (WBHO, Bayside, Transnet, retail rollout PCs) reject generic files.
- CIDB register: roughly 108,000 Grade 1 and 21,000 Grade 2 to 9 contractors (CIDB to Parliament, Q4 2024). Every one of them needs files; the Grade 2 to 5 band working for principal contractors is our buyer.
- Current prices: consultant-compiled file R2,500 to R20,000 and 48 to 72 hours (ConRisk, MySafetyFile comparison). Template generators R400 to R2,000 per file. SHEQ Warehouse "2026 package" R3,150 to R3,950.
- The number one rejection cause cited by practitioners: inconsistency across documents (project name, scope, contractor details, unsigned appointments). Our QA pass is built for exactly this.
- Nobody we found sells a subscription. Incumbents advertise "no monthly fees" as a feature, which tells us they sell to one-off buyers and that the buyer thinks per file. That is a warning as much as an opening: a subscription only sticks if cancelling costs the customer something real. Ours does, because the live file link and the vault go dark. Rapid Safety Files' "Compliance Rationale Report" claim could not be verified today; assume the capability exists.
- Our buyer is the contractor doing 2 to 10 sites a month, who today pays R5,000 to R20,000 a month in files and consultant time, and the SACPCMP consultant who produces those files.

## 4. Offer and pricing (ZAR, VAT exclusive)

| Plan | Price | Who | Includes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reviewed File (launch product) | R1,950 once | Any contractor, first 60 days | Full spec-matched file pack, checked by a human before release, 24-hour turnaround, live share link for 90 days |
| Pro | R1,499/mo + R499 per active site | Subcontractor running 1 to 10 live sites | Unlimited file generation, vault, 5 users, white-labelled output, live PC share links with audit log, weekly register and toolbox packs per site, expiry tracker |
| Consultant | R2,999/mo + R299 per client company | SACPCMP CHS consultants | Multi-company workspace, their branding, their review and release step, 20% reseller margin on Pro referrals |
| Annual prepay | 2 months free | Any plan | Cash up front, churn protection |

Starter at R799 is gone. It priced us against MySafetyFile's R400 and would lose. Pro at a flat R1,999 unlimited gave our best customers the most margin for free; per-active-site pricing tracks the value and makes the subscription behave like the site does.

**Founding member offer (first 20):** Pro base fee waived for 6 months, pay only R499 per active site. Testimonial file and permission to name the principal contractor in return.

**Path to R50k MRR:** 15 Pro accounts averaging 3 active sites (R2,996 each = R44,940) + 2 Consultant accounts with 8 clients (R5,391 each = R10,782) = R55,722. Reviewed File revenue on top is cash, not MRR, and we do not count it as MRR.

**Unit economics:** Claude generation cost per full 30-document pack is about R75 to R80 with prompt caching (Opus 5.5 at $4/$20 per million tokens, roughly 90k output tokens plus a cached 40k prefix, plus the schedule and QA passes), about R165 uncached. Human review on the launch product is about 45 minutes per file, roughly R400 at contracted rates, against R1,950. Paystack takes 2.9% + R1. Hosting about R600/mo (Vercel Pro is required for long-running generation functions). Gross margin about 75% on reviewed files, above 90% on subscriptions. Fair-use cap: 15 new file packs per month on Pro, then R299 per additional pack, so an account cannot go underwater on generation cost.

## 5. Product scope for the 2-day build

The technical review cut this to what one agent can ship in 48 hours. The ordering de-risks the two hard integrations (document rendering and long-running generation) before any screens are built.

**Hours 0 to 24: a working generator**
1. Supabase project, schema, row-level security, magic-link auth. Next.js app on Vercel. Repo: mbullardct-svg/AIBusiness.
2. Document engine first: Claude emits a structured document model (headings, paragraphs, tables, signature blocks); two deterministic renderers produce DOCX (docx library) and PDF (react-pdf), merged with pdf-lib, zipped, stored privately, served by signed links. Tested with stub content before any AI.
3. Generation runner: a job and step table, a self-chaining Vercel function that checkpoints every document, and a cron sweeper for stale jobs. A 30-document pack takes 15 to 25 minutes and must survive a function timeout.
4. Agent pipeline: Haiku 5.5 reads the PC's specification PDF into a requirements register; Opus 5.5 drafts each of the 32 sections from one code-injected fact sheet (company, site, PC, scope, dates, appointments) so particulars are never retyped by the model; then the responsibility schedule and gap register; then a consistency pass over the fact sheet and per-document summaries. The legal register is a curated dataset, not model output.
5. Minimal vault: company particulars and logo, appointments as a fixed checklist, people as a flat table, uploads as a document list. Equipment registers and competency matrices wait for week 2.
6. New Site File wizard, dashboard, gap register with "to be supplied by you" items.
7. Review gate: every pack lands in a review queue. Michael or the contracted reviewer approves, edits or sends back before the customer can download. Self-serve release is a per-account flag we flip later.
8. First full run against the Transnet TPT specification by hour 12, compared line by line to our August file.

**Hours 24 to 48: a business**
9. Paystack plans and subscriptions in test mode (ZAR, card, 3D Secure; no native trials or proration, so the founding offer is its own plan), webhook with signature verification, plan entitlements. EFT invoice path with admin "mark paid" so founding members can pay before KYC completes.
10. Live site share link: read-only, per site, with an audit log of who opened it and when. This is the retention mechanism, so it ships in the 48 hours.
11. Landing page, pricing, Reviewed File order flow, sample pack download, terms (drafting and compilation tool; employer appoints and signs), privacy (POPIA position in section 6).
12. Custom domain, Resend transactional email, rate limits (one running job per company, plan quota, daily cap), Supabase security advisor pass, end-to-end test as a fresh user.
13. Outreach: drafted emails and WhatsApp copy for the first 40 contacts and the PC scorecard invitation, ready for your approval.

**Deferred to week 2 (not needed to sell the first file):** weekly register and toolbox packs, expiry tracker emails, white-label branding, consultant multi-company workspace, PC scorecard page, error monitoring, equipment register, competency matrix.

## 6. Stack and running cost

| Layer | Choice | Monthly cost |
|---|---|---|
| App | Next.js 15 on Vercel Pro (long-running functions, per-minute cron) | ~R370 |
| Data | Supabase (new project, eu-west-2 London) | ~R190 |
| AI | Anthropic API: Opus 5.5 drafting, Haiku 5.5 extraction, prompt caching on | ~R80 per file pack |
| Billing | Paystack (ZAR subscriptions, 3D Secure) | 2.9% + R1 per transaction |
| Email | Resend (free to 3,000/mo) | R0 |
| Domain | sitefile.ai via Vercel ($160 for 2 years) or sitefileai.com ($11.25/yr) | once-off |

POPIA position. The vault holds ID numbers and medical certificates, which are special personal information under sections 26 and 27. Design rules from day one: (1) the model never receives ID numbers, medical content or certificate scans; it drafts from names, roles and competencies only, so Anthropic in the US processes no special PI; (2) uploads are stored encrypted in Supabase London with row-level security and signed, expiring download links; (3) operator agreements under section 21 with Supabase, Vercel and Anthropic are referenced in the privacy policy; (4) section 72 grounds for cross-border transfer are documented; (5) Information Officer registration and a PAIA manual are done in the first 30 days; (6) cold outreach goes to business contacts we have a relationship with, not scraped lists, and every email carries an opt-out, which is the section 69 position. We take legal advice on whether section 57 prior authorisation is triggered before we store medicals for third-party companies; until then medicals are the customer's upload and we hold them as operator, not responsible party.

## 7. Go-to-market (first 30 days)

1. **Our own sites first (days 1 to 10):** the next five BCS files (Transnet sections, Toyota, Tongaat Hulett Botswana, the retail rollouts) are produced on SiteFile and submitted as normal. We learn what the PC safety officers bounce before any third party pays us.
2. **Principal contractors as the channel (week 1):** Bayside Engineering and the two or three PC safety officers who know us get the free scorecard and the share link. We ask them to point their subcontractor base at us. This is distribution, not an afterthought.
3. **Our own network (week 1 to 2):** our subs and suppliers, North Coast Aircon, electrical and painting contractors on the Boxer and Pedros rollouts, SAPCA pest control members. 40 named contacts, Reviewed File first, founding Pro offer second.
4. **Consultant channel (week 3 onward):** SACPCMP-registered CHS officers who compile files for clients. Positioned as their production tool with their review step and their name on the file, not as their replacement. Expect this channel to be slow and sceptical.
5. **Search (from day 30):** Google Ads on "safety file" terms, content pages per trade and per PC specification. Incumbents own organic; we buy the top of the funnel until the content ranks.

## 9. Honest view on the timeline

- **48 hours:** platform live, generating files behind the review gate, taking Reviewed File orders and founding sign-ups, invoicing by EFT. Paystack live payments follow KYC.
- **Day 10:** five BCS files produced on the platform and submitted to real PCs. This is the quality proof.
- **Day 30, base case:** 4 to 6 founding accounts plus 8 to 12 Reviewed Files. MRR R6k to R12k, cash R15k to R25k.
- **Day 90, base case:** MRR R20k to R30k. **Stretch:** R50k if two PCs adopt the share link and push their subcontractor base to us.
- **R50k MRR, base case:** month 5 to 7, conditional on month-3 logo retention above 85%.
- **Kill criteria:** fewer than 3 principal contractor acceptances of SiteFile output by day 45, or month-2 retention under 80%. Either one and we stop and redirect the stack to the FMCG bird and pest compliance module.

R50k in two days is not achievable for any new business with real customers, and I will not model it as if it were. What is achievable is a live, selling product in two days, cash from reviewed files in week one, and R50k MRR on the five to seven month line, with a credible shot at 90 days if the principal contractor channel opens. I would rather tell you that now than on day 3.

## 10. Risks and how we handle them

| Risk | Handling |
|---|---|
| A PC bounces a SiteFile pack and word gets round Durban sites, with BCS's name attached | First five files go onto BCS's own sites. Review gate on the first 20 files. Self-serve release only after three PC acceptances. Sample files published for PCs to inspect. |
| Competence and signatures | SACPCMP registration is required for client's agents (CR 5(5)) and CHS officers (CR 8(5)), not for compiling a file. Terms position the platform as a drafting and compilation tool; the employer makes appointments in writing and signs. Appointment letters are rendered unsigned with signature blocks, never pre-signed. No marketing copy claims the file "proves" compliance. |
| Paystack KYC delay | EFT invoicing from day 1. MRR starts before card billing. |
| Model drift or hallucinated regulation citations | Legal register is a fixed, human-curated dataset in the database; the model fills facts, it does not invent law. QA pass checks citations against the register. |
| POPIA on medical data and ID numbers | See section 6. Model never sees special PI. Encrypted storage, RLS, signed links, retention policy, operator agreements, Information Officer registration. |
| Incident on a site using our file, DoL section 24 investigation reads our documents | Review gate, human sign-off, PI insurance, new Pty Ltd within 60 days, terms that place the duty where the Act places it: on the employer. |
| Consumer Protection Act for sole-proprietor customers | No 12-month lock-ins; monthly plans cancel on 20 business days' notice; annual prepay is optional with a clear renewal notice. No "Transnet standard" claims without Transnet's consent. |
| You are the bottleneck on sales | Outreach is drafted, sequenced and tracked by me. You approve and take the calls. |

Approve to proceed with: the name SiteFile AI, the domain purchase, the stack above, and the pricing. Reply "go" and provide items 2 to 4 in section 8 as you get to them. I start the build the moment you approve.
